subject.title: fix(config): improve validation error messages with line numbers, bracket paths, and received values

question: Should terminal validation print effective env/include-resolved values for non-sensitive config paths, and which open PR should own the shared bracket-formatting implementation?
rationale: Using authored values is misleading, but switching to effective values expands the terminal disclosure boundary across plugin-owned and environment-resolved configuration; repository policy and the competing branch do not determine that permanent contract automatically.

options.title: Effective values, fail closed
options.body: Use the effective pre-default config for received hints, restrict printable values and paths conservatively, add env/include/plugin-secret tests, and consolidate bracket formatting into the selected canonical branch.

options.title: Drop received-value hints
options.body: Land only line numbers and bracketed display paths, avoiding a new value-disclosure contract while retaining most of the usability improvement.

options.title: Split the work
options.body: Land the narrow bracket-path PR and keep line-location plus received-value behavior in a separate owner-sponsored follow-up.

recommendation.title: Effective values, fail closed
recommendation.body: Use the effective pre-default config for received hints, restrict printable values and paths conservatively, add env/include/plugin-secret tests, and consolidate bracket formatting into the selected canonical branch.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work owns the source/resolved/runtime snapshot distinction that determines which value is authoritative and safe to display.
